item.title: Family support keeps Daunivalu motivated ahead of Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 15-year-old basketball player Nyssa Daunivalu says the support of her family helps her overcome difficult moments as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. Originally from Gau, the St Joseph's Secondary School student says she sometimes feels demoralised after a bad game or training session.
item.content:encoded:
15-year-old basketball player Nyssa Daunivalu says the support of her family helps her overcome difficult moments as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

Originally from Gau, the St Joseph's Secondary School student says she sometimes feels demoralised after a bad game or training session.

She says the support and encouragement of her family helps her overcome these challenges and stay motivated to keep improving as a player.

Daunivalu says preparations for the Games are going well, with the team working hard and building on the chemistry developed during last year’s Under-17 Championship in Newcastle.

She says the players are familiar with one another’s playing styles, which has helped them work well together.

The 15-year-old also balances her basketball commitments with schoolwork by setting aside two hours to study after school before attending training.

Daunivalu has thanked those supporting her journey and encouraged other young people who dream of playing basketball to keep working hard and pursuing their goals.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from October 30 to November 13.

item.content:encoded:
Tevita Ikanivere will Captain the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as they prepare for the Japan Centennial Test under the guidance of their new head coach, South African Jake White, who led the Springboks to victory at the 2007 Rugby World Cup.

Ikanivere, who has been a key figure in Fiji’s forward pack, will play a central role in the team’s preparations as they look to deliver a strong performance against Japan.

The squad features experienced forwards Peni Ravai, Mesake Doge, Samuela Tawake, Isoa Nasilasila, Mesake Vocevoce and Motikiai Murray, who are expected to provide strength, physicality and leadership up front.

They will be supported by Kitione Salawa, Isoa Tuwai, Meli Tuni, Penaia Cakobau and Kavaia Tagivetaua, adding depth and competition within the forward pack.

In the backs, Frank Lomani, Ben Volavola, Sam Wye, Kemu Valetini and Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula are among the players expected to play important roles in directing Fiji’s attack.

The squad also includes experienced campaigners Terio Tamani, Joji Nasova, Isikeli Rabitu and Maleli Nauvasi as the Flying Fijians look to combine attacking flair with composure and consistency.

Meanwhile, the selection provides opportunities for emerging players to make their mark on the international stage, with several players identified as potential debutants in the squad announcement.

The inclusion of new talent alongside established internationals reflects the team's efforts to build depth and strengthen competition for places within the national side.

The Flying Fijians will be looking to put their preparations into action against Japan , with the Test providing an important opportunity to assess the squad ahead of their upcoming international commitments.

Fiji will face Japan next Saturday at 5.50pm.

item.title: 16-year-old Suka ready to make family and Fiji proud at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: Young basketballer Zara Suka is ready to make her family and Fiji proud as she prepares to represent the country at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. Originally from Yadrana, Lakeba, Lau, Suka says her preparations are going well, with the team building strong connections and working together ahead of the Games.
item.content:encoded:
Young basketballer Zara Suka is ready to make her family and Fiji proud as she prepares to represent the country at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

Originally from Yadrana, Lakeba, Lau, Suka says her preparations are going well, with the team building strong connections and working together ahead of the Games.

The 16-year-old says her basketball journey began at the age of six, and she has continued to develop her passion for the sport over the past 10 years.

She says one of the challenges she faces as an athlete is learning to put a bad game behind her and focus on the next match.

She has thanked her supporters for their encouragement and says she hopes to continue improving as a player.

Meanwhile, her father, former Fiji Bati player Ratu Suka, says he is extremely proud to see his daughter represent Fiji on the international stage.

He says Zara has been playing basketball for 10 years, and it has been encouraging to watch her growth and development in the sport.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.

item.title: 15-member squad named for inaugural PacificAus Sports Netball challenge next month
item.description: Netball Fiji has named a 15-member squad to represent the country at the inaugural PacificAus Sports Netball Challenge 2026 in Brisbane, Australia. The squad features locally based netballers who will have the opportunity to gain international experience, strengthen their skills and further develop their performance at the international level.
item.content:encoded:
Netball Fiji has named a 15-member squad to represent the country at the inaugural PacificAus Sports Netball Challenge 2026 in Brisbane, Australia.

The squad features locally based netballers who will have the opportunity to gain international experience, strengthen their skills and further develop their performance at the international level.

The selected players are Esther Dawai, Mereoni Taqiri, Kiana Toganivalu, Sereana Viriviri, Seini Naulia, Susana Rasaubale, Elenoa Rasaubale, Tuipulotu Vulimailaucala, Anatolia Nuku, Dimere Rarabota, Sainimere Tagicakiverata, Lydia Tavesivesi, Yvonne Nalewabau, Eseta Waqaira and Ateca Buli.

The inaugural challenge will be hosted by Netball Australia, and will run from the 23rd to the 28th of next month.
